correctness.rationale: Geometric smoothness on the blowup is equivalent to smoothness of the representing plane cubic: a singularity off the centers persists, and multiplicity at least two at a center gives an exceptional component of the anticanonical divisor meeting the strict transform (or a multiple exceptional component). A smooth plane cubic, in contrast, lifts isomorphically. Euler's identity in characteristic two identifies its singularities with the common projective zeros of the three quadratic partials. The partials have no common projective zero exactly when their degree-four multiples span all degree-four forms (regular sequence Hilbert series, and evaluation at a common zero for the converse). Exact rank enumeration returned 23 masks and 12 all-smooth binary pencils; coordinate permutations and Cremona reversal give the two six-element orbits under the split automorphism group, with the stated point multisets. The fresh exact replay checked all 12 pencils in F_64, in each case finding the three centers with distinct tangent directions for the two generators and six residual points in one length-six Frobenius orbit. Smooth cubics are geometrically integral, and distinct pencil members have no common component, so the six residual points exhaust the intersection number (-K_S)^2=6 after blowup and each is simple. Evaluating at a rational surface point would give a pencil in the kernel of any proposed all-smooth net, contrary to rational-base-point exclusion. Exhausting dimension-three subspaces by smooth triples independently gave zero. The statement is about H^0(S,-K_S), not the unrestricted space of plane cubics.
residual_risks: The result concerns rational members over F_2 and geometric smoothness of each such member, not smoothness at every geometric parameter or other del Pezzo forms. Enumeration is exact but not proof-assistant certification.

evidence: The degree-seven Finding covers every all-smooth pencil after the first two blowups, with geometrically reduced length-seven bases and only partitions (7), (2,5), (1,6). It also excludes all-smooth anticanonical nets in its larger section space.

The quadric and degree-five results are neighboring calculations only. The general existence papers do not give the split degree-six arithmetic, and unrestricted all-smooth plane nets over F_2 do exist.

evidence: The third center is a common rational base point on the split degree-seven surface; among the three partitions only (1,6) has such a point. Reducedness means local length one at the rational point, so the local equations of two generators have independent differentials in the regular surface local ring. Their strict transforms meet the new exceptional curve in different tangent points; the unique residual degree-six point is unaffected by blowup.

A vector space of cubics through three fixed centers is contained in the space through the first two, with smoothness preserved. Alternatively, differential evaluation at even one common marked point is a linear map to a two-dimensional cotangent space, and any all-smooth subspace must inject under that map.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Thus the reduced Frobenius-six assertion is an immediate consequence for every such pencil, not an unrecorded refined invariant requiring a new elimination. Both the sharp dimension bound and the orbit classification also follow with only restriction and direct table evaluation.

evidence: A pencil on the split surface is a plane cubic pencil through a fixed ordered-coordinate frame, with a change of coordinates allowed to permute the three centers. Smoothness matches the plane presentation for anticanonical divisors, as checked above.

The ambient table has exactly 336 pencils with three rational base points, in two PGL_3(F_2)-orbits of size 168. If those three base points were collinear, restriction of the pencil to their line would have image of dimension at most one: the restrictions are binary cubics divisible by the product of the three point factors. Some nonzero member would contain that line and not be geometrically smooth. Thus every three-point base set in the table is a noncollinear triple.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: PGL_3(F_2) is transitive on the 28 unordered noncollinear triples. Each ambient free orbit restricts over the chosen triple to one orbit of size 6 under its stabilizer S_3. There are exactly 12 pencils before considering Cremona. The computed point-count multisets of the two indexed representatives are different, so the full group D12 cannot merge these two six-orbits; both stabilizers have order 2. This is a restriction of an actual complete marked classification, not similarity of title or count.
